"Selama ada aerasi atau sirkulasi, ikan semestinya aman semalaman." slightly generalises: the facts apply this to short outages under two hours.
"Memindahkan ikan antarakuarium ... terlalu cepat" – the facts say moving fish should be a last resort, not that doing it "too quickly" is the problem.

"Akuarium besar lebih lama menahan suhunya" and the other general points are supported; the 'Mulailah sebelum ikan megap-megap' advice is supported.

"Kematian biasanya karena sesak napas" fine, but "Ikan yang sakit masih sangat muda atau sudah tua, karena kelompok ini paling sering mati" is a mild extension of the fact (high death rates), acceptable.
"Lanjutkan pengobatan cukup lama, karena hanya tahap dinospora ... yang bisa dibunuh obat" is a reasonable inference, but the intro says velvet looks "kuning keemasan atau seperti karat" – fine.
"Sumber yang sama mencantumkan penambahan garam akuarium sebagai langkah berikutnya" – the facts list salt as step 5 in the same source; OK. The guide says the dose is not given, which is true.
"Redupkan atau matikan lampu. Ada perbedaan pendapat" – supported by the facts.

"Untuk obat yang dosisnya tidak tercantum di tabel, ikuti label produknya" – a generic rule from the writer, not a claim from the facts (the facts do not give doses for methylene blue, formalin or acriflavine).
"Dinospora mungkin bisa menyebar antarakuarium ... lewat percikan air" – supported.
"Pada kasus lanjut, ikan mati karena kekurangan oksigen akibat insang yang membusuk" – supported by the facts (gill necrosis).
"Ikan yang sakit masih sangat muda atau sudah tua" is listed under 'Kapan harus khawatir', a section the facts do not give, though it is built from the facts.
"Betta liar dan ikan blackwater" – supported. "Penyakit ini bisa tertukar" – supported.
The table's "Sumbernya tidak memberi jadwal" for quinine and homemade copper is accurate.

Minor: step 5 "Tambahkan garam akuarium, kecuali untuk ikan yang tidak tahan garam" gives no dose for the aquarium salt, and the exception is the writer's own addition. The facts give only the salt-bath dose and the Co-op method.
Minor: "Penyakit ini sering dikira jamur" is drawn from the claim about Vietnamese sources and stated a bit more broadly than the facts.
"keluarkan karbon atau resin penyerap" – facts say remove carbon or Purigen; "resin penyerap" is a generalization of Purigen.

"Antibiotik di akuarium karantina/pengobatan, bukan di akuarium utama" – "bukan di akuarium utama" is added; facts only say antibiotics in a treatment tank.

"Kalau ada tanda busuk mulut (columnaris)... ikan yang terinfeksi harus dipindah ke akuarium karantina" – facts say hospital tank; fine, but the "Kapan harus waspada" section is largely the writer's framing (e.g., "Busuk sudah mendekati pangkal sirip" as an alert trigger).
"Bakteri ini sering hidup normal di lendir kulit ikan atau di air" – merges two sources; acceptable.
"Ikuti dosis pada label produk yang dibeli" for erythromycin/methylene blue – facts give no dose for these; this is the writer's rule.

"Sumber lain menyarankan obat baru dipakai kalau ikan tidak membaik..." is fine, but "Pilih produk yang tidak mengandung pewarna" is attributed correctly. No problem here.

"Perlu dibedakan juga dengan busuk mulut (columnaris)... ikan yang terinfeksi sebaiknya dipindah ke akuarium pengobatan": the facts say hospital tank; the guide frames columnaris as a differential diagnosis, which the facts do not state (minor generalization).

"Garam non-iodium" – the facts never say non-iodized salt; invented specification.

"Pindahkan ikan yang suka menggigit... lalu" fine, but "Obat baru dipakai kalau kondisi ikan tidak membaik" in the intro is presented as the vet's view; it is actually Mytour's advice (minor attribution blur).
"lepas karbon aktif atau resin penyerap" – facts say remove carbon or Purigen; "resin penyerap" is a generalization of the product.
"Malachite green ... Pakai sesuai label" – the facts give no dose or label guidance for it; also no caveat given about it.
"Bakteri ini biasanya memang hidup di air atau di lendir kulit ikan" – merges two sources; acceptable but combined.

"Pakan yang kurang baik dan stres" and "akar tanaman yang lunak" fine; "tetapi hanya kalau... obati ikan yang sakit di akuarium karantina" in FAQ – the facts do not advise treating in a quarantine tank as a way to protect invertebrates (invented recommendation).
"Sebagai patokan, ganti air tiap 3 hari ... 4 L" is supported, but the guide's "Pembusukan sudah mendekati pangkal sirip" under 'when to worry' is the writer's inference.

"Tes air... dokter hewan akuatik... hubungi dokter hewan" fine; "Kematian bisa terjadi dalam beberapa hari begitu bakteri masuk ke darah" slightly reworded but OK.

"Obat jamur siap pakai ... jadi ikuti label produk yang Anda beli" — writer's rule for undosed products, acceptable.
"Pengobatan berlebihan ... penyebab yang belum dibereskan bisa membuat infeksi datang lagi" — mostly supported; the facts only link overtreatment to recurring infection.

Intro claims "Jamur pada ikan biasanya disebabkan Saprolegnia" and the 'Apa itu jamur' text says "organisme berbentuk benang yang umum ada di air tawar dan payau" — supported, but 'biasanya' is a mild generalisation.
The guide's table says the salt/3 ppt row lists source 3 and 'Rendaman garam' source labels as numbers; the 'Sumber' column is fine.
"Catfish ... dan ada ikan yang tidak tahan kenaikan kadar garam sekecil apa pun" — facts say some fish will not tolerate 'even slightly raised salinity'; acceptable.
The salt dip fact (30 g/L for 0.5–10 min, remove fish in distress) is omitted; this is an omission, not an error.
"Luka di kulit atau insang yang masih dangkal pun bisa berakibat fatal" — supported, but repeated in 'Kapan harus khawatir' with the added "Jangan tunggu sampai parah", a mild unsupported advisory.
The "Kapan harus khawatir" section and the line "Telur yang tidak dibuahi ... karena jamur menyebar dari telur mati ke telur sehat" are supported.
Overall small unsupported generalities only; no invented doses found.

"Celup garam untuk ikan air tawar (tujuannya membasmi parasit luar)" with 30 g/L is placed in the antifungal treatment table, but the facts give this dip only for removing external parasites, not for fungus. The guide notes this, but listing it as a treatment option still implies it is an antifungal dose.
"Bersihkan kotoran sebelum mengobati" is not in the facts. They only say chemicals react with organic matter and lower the effective dose.
"Perlukah karbon aktif dilepas saat mengobati? Perlu." Removal of carbon is an inference. The facts only say carbon absorbs the medication.
"Kalau lukanya tidak membaik ... cek lagi apakah ada parasit atau columnaris" is advice the facts do not give. They only say Saprolegnia often co-occurs with columnaris or parasites.

"Apakah jamur pada ikan menular ke ikan lain?" is answered with an inference. The facts do not discuss contagion between adult fish. They say only that spores are present everywhere and that it spreads between eggs.
"obati jamurnya dengan garam, methylene blue (untuk telur), atau obat jamur sesuai label" is partly the writer's rule. "Sesuai label" is acceptable for products with no dose in the facts.
"Di kalangan hobiis sebutan 'jamur' sudah terlanjur umum" is an unsupported generality.
Title and text say "Mudik Lebaran" while the facts are about Tet (Lunar New Year) travel; this holiday framing is not in the facts.
"Apa pun pilihannya, risiko terbesar justru pakan berlebih": the facts name sitter overfeeding as the main risk, not overfeeding in general for every option.
"Orang yang belum kenal akuarium memang sering kebanyakan memberi pakan": this is supported, but the guide presents it as a general claim.
"Kalau bisa, minta seseorang mengecek feeder setiap beberapa hari": this is supported, but the guide places it in the feeder steps in a slightly different way.
"Tetra, rasbora, guppy, dan corydoras": "Tetra" is read as the fish group, but the facts also name Tetra the brand elsewhere. This is only a minor ambiguity.
The guide adds the "Ganti air dan bersihkan filter" step as a grouped item and tells the reader to "Buang daun tanaman yang mati". The facts support this.
"Untuk lebih dari seminggu, semua sepakat ikan jangan dibiarkan tanpa pakan" - overstated consensus; only one source says not to leave unfed on trips over a week.
"Takar pakan per hari di kotak obat mingguan" - facts say only a pill box with pre-measured daily food; "weekly" is added.
"Pakan beku lebih cocok diberikan oleh orang yang dititipi, ditakar per kubus" - the facts only say frozen cubes are cleaner and easier to portion; this is partly an inference.

"Pakan berlebih jauh lebih berbahaya daripada ikan yang terlewat makan" - the facts say overfeeding by helpers kills more fish, which the guide generalises to all overfeeding.
"Nyalakan lagi filter ... cek sekali lagi bahwa filternya benar-benar jalan" - the facts do not say to double-check this.
"Kalau tetap ingin memakainya, uji dulu seminggu sebelum berangkat" - the facts support testing about 1 week before leaving, but only as a general step.

"Penyakit seperti mata turun, sisik berdiri, dan tutup insang miring banyak dikaitkan dengan kualitas air, ruang yang sempit, dan cara memberi pakan" – overgeneralised; drop eye causes are disputed and mostly not water quality.

"Kalau air keran Anda mengandung kloramin..." - the chloramine point is not tied to cleaning glass in the facts; it is off-topic padding.
"Kerak putih di garis air itu apa, dan berbahaya tidak?" - the facts never say whether limescale is dangerous. The answer implies it is harmless or not, with no support.

"Angka yang lebih besar itu ditujukan untuk keadaan toksin sudah lama terkumpul tanpa sesiapa memantau. Angka yang lebih kecil pula untuk tangki yang sedang diuji dan dipantau." - invented explanation; the facts do not say why the figures differ.
"tetapi tukar sedikit sahaja jika beza suhu antara air baru dengan air tangki besar" - slightly garbled; facts say keep the change small if the temperature difference is large.
"Cabut plag penapis sepenuhnya... Jika tidak, air tangki boleh tersedut keluar" in the FAQ generalised: siphoning applies only to overflow filters (the guide notes this elsewhere, so it is minor).
"Pastikan bilik ditutup" is an interpretation of 'keep the room closed' and is only loosely supported.
"Jangan ganggu ikan" and "Mula menambah oksigen sebelum ikan mula megap" are supported, but the pairing 'UPS lebih sesuai untuk penapis' is an inference beyond the facts.
"Botol air panas juga boleh digunakan" - the facts say hot-water bottles are placed in the tank; the guide mixes this with the bottles-in-the-tank method, a minor blur.
"Penyakit bintik putih (white spot)" - the facts say 'Ich', which is fine, but the statement 'Ikan yang lembap' is a mistranslation of 'sluggish' (minor).
"Gunakan mengikut label produk yang dibeli" (oxygen tablets): the facts give no dose, so this is the writer's own rule, not a claim. Minor.

"Lebih baik guna UPS untuk penapis" and "pemanas bervoltan rendah seperti 10 watt": the facts say only that a 10 W heater draws far less than a 100 W one. They do not recommend a UPS for the filter over the heater, and they never call it a 'low-voltage' heater. Voltage is the wrong term; it is wattage.

"Lebih seminggu ... Minta kedai ikan hiasan" in the table: the facts give this advice for outages of more than a week, so it is supported. It is placed in the duration table next to other rows, which is fine.
"Kebanyakan ikan boleh bertahan sekurang-kurangnya kira-kira seminggu tanpa makanan" (FAQ): the facts say 'about a week' and 'days or even weeks'. 'At least' is a slight shift.
"pastikan bilik ditutup" in the 4–8 hour row: the facts say 'keep the room closed' with no reason. This matches the source, but the guide adds no explanation.

"Elektrik terputus sekejap begini biasanya tidak menjadi masalah walaupun tanpa penapis" and "ikan sepatutnya boleh bertahan semalaman": the overnight claim in the facts depends on aeration or circulation being provided. The guide states it with that condition, so it is acceptable.
"Kalau anda tiada di rumah... tukar 25–50% air": supported by the facts, but it sits beside the 10–30% advice with no reconciliation. It is not invented.
Opening: "Teruskan rawatan sehingga kitaran hidup parasit itu putus" is not in the facts (facts say continue until no symptoms / about a week).
"Kuprum sulfat (rendaman)... Sehingga 10 hari" is fine, but "kuprum sulfat ... gunakan mengikut label produk yang dibeli" for the listed drugs is the writer's rule, acceptable.
"Dinospora: berenang bebas untuk mencari ikan baharu" - slight embellishment, not stated in facts.
"Velvet atau penyakit bintik putih? ... Tidak" - the FAQ answer "Tidak" is implied only; facts just say it can be confused with ich.

"Kuprum lebih toksik dalam air berasid, jadi kuprum terkelat lebih sesuai" is supported; but "Turutan langkah menurut sumber 6" puts the temperature raise and a 'carbon removal reason' in a different order than the facts' listed steps (change water, raise temp, dim lights, remove carbon, salt) - minor.
"Selamatkah kuprum untuk udang dan siput? Tidak." - a blunt conclusion beyond the facts, though consistent with the toxicity data.
"Ikan keli anchor catfish" - facts say only 'anchor catfish'; the 'keli' gloss is minor.
"tumbuhan akuatik" as a copper-sensitive group is an acceptable rendering of 'plants'.

"Suhu jatuh kira-kira 8 °C dalam masa sejam, atau air di bawah kira-kira 23 °C": facts say about 15°F and 73°F; the conversions are approximate and 15°F ≈ 8°C, 73°F ≈ 23°C, which is roughly fine, but this is a rewrite of the units.

"Sumber 4 menyebut suhu melebihi kira-kira 29 °C memendekkan kitaran hidup": facts say heat above 84°F, which is about 29°C. This is okay but 'sumber 4 ... 30 hari pada suhu kira-kira 29 °C atau lebih' is also converted.
"1 cawan bagi setiap kira-kira 76 liter air": facts say 1 cup per 20 gallons; the metric conversion is the writer's own.
"Tambah garam akuarium mengikut label produk (sumber 6 tidak memberi dos)": the dose-by-label rule for salt is the writer's own; the facts give no such product.
"Sumber 4 merawat ikan laga liar dengan kuprum terkelat selama 30 dari": garbled text, and the guide implies Mardel CopperSafe for 30 days at 'kira-kira 29 °C', where the facts say 84°F or above.

"Sumber 0 dan sumber 1 menyebut parasit memerlukan cahaya": the facts say Aquarium Co-op and Wikipedia (source 0) say the parasite needs light. Source 1 only says 7 days of darkness helps alongside drugs, so attributing the 'needs light' claim to source 1 is unsupported.

"Selepas itu rawat tangki utama dan tangki kuarantin sekali" and "Ikan yang dijangkiti anak ikan yang sangat kecil": minor paraphrases that turn the facts slightly (the intro says the parasite is still in the substrate even if the fish look recovered, which is supported only loosely).
"Menurut sumber 3, kaedah air masin ini sepatutnya berkesan": the facts attribute this to FAO and cite source 3. This is acceptable.

"Velvet nampak seperti debu halus keemasan atau karat, bukan bintik-bintik yang jelas": the facts give no description of ich spots, so this contrast is the writer's own. The guide also says "Penyakit bintik putih pula berupa bintik-bintik" without support.
"Kadar kematian mereka tinggi" / "kematian akibat lemas" are supported. The 'Bila perlu risau' section adds advice not in the facts.
"Gentian violet: disapu terus pada luka, mengikut label" – facts only say dabbed on the lesion; 'mengikut label' is the writer's addition (minor).
"keluarkan karbon atau media penjerap yang seumpamanya" – facts say carbon or Purigen; generalised wording.
"Reput sirip ... sering dilihat pada ikan laga dan ikan mas koki" in the intro is ok, but "Asingkan ikan penggigit sirip atau yang suka bergaduh" is slight extension (facts say remove them).
"Kereputan ... Kanamycin ... Ia juga boleh dicampur ke dalam makanan" fine; but "Gunakan mengikut label" for malachite green is the writer's rule with no dose in facts (minor).
"Kepercayaan ... tidak disokong oleh sebarang rujukan" – facts say only that the claim lacks a citation on Wikipedia; slightly overstated.
"columnaris (yang juga dikenali sebagai reput mulut)" – facts say mouth rot (columnaris); acceptable but equated.
Intro says reput sirip "biasanya oleh bakteria" and "boleh merebak ke badan" – supported; the line about tank cleaning being 'menyatakan' that doctor and guide agree is supported.
"ubat hanya digunakan jika ikan tidak pulih" in the intro is attributed to the aquatic vet. That 'medicate only if no improvement' advice comes from Mytour, not the vet.

"Ikan yang dijangkiti patut dipindahkan ke tangki rawatan" is placed under columnaris. The facts say columnaris fish go to a hospital tank, which is nearly the same. The guide is also loose in presenting 'reput mulut' as a KanaPlex-listed item.
"Lebih baik lagi, rawat ikan yang sakit di tangki berasingan" in the shrimp/snail FAQ is the writer's own recommendation. The facts do not say this.
"Kematian boleh berlaku dalam beberapa hari apabila bakteria masuk ke dalam darah" is slightly twisted. The facts say mortality can come within days and rises sharply once bacteria reach the blood.
"Reput sirip ialah jangkitan, biasanya oleh bakteria" and "Satu panduan menyebut tangki tanpa penapis" are small paraphrases. They are acceptable and only minor.
"Bila perlu risau" is an invented section that adds interpretation, such as the claim that a fish going dark is a worry sign. The facts do not list these as warning triggers.
"Sumber tidak sepakat tentang penggunaan ubat" is the writer's framing of the sources as disagreeing. The facts do not say that.
"pengeluar satu produk kanamycin ... khusus untuk produk tersebut" is hedging added by the writer. It is harmless.
"kualiti air yang teruk, termasuk air kotor" and "kecederaan, contohnya akibat bergaduh atau digigit" are reasonable reworkings of the facts.
The "Garam" table is placed under treatment. The facts give routine salt as 1–3 g/L but do not tie it to fin rot. The 'Rutin' duration is the writer's addition.
The intro says fin rot makes the edges "makin pendek" (shorter). The facts only describe ragged or discolored fins, plus loss of tissue in later stages. This is a small embellishment.

"Ini maklumat tentang toleransi ikan, bukan rawatan reput sirip" (about 1–3 g/L routine salt) is the writer's own framing. The facts list the 1–3 g/L figure under treatment and don't say it is not a treatment. It is a small interpretation, not an invented claim.

The table gives the dose for erythromycin, methylene blue, malachite green and gentian violet as "ikut label produk yang dibeli". The facts give no dose for these, so this is the writer's own rule and not a claim from the sources.

"Malachite green disenaraikan berkesan dalam sesetengah kes. Ikut label." and "Gentian violet disapu terus pada luka. Ikut label." – labelled as dosing by label is acceptable, but "sering menyerang ikan laga dan ikan mas koki" is fine; minor.

"Ubat hanya digunakan jika ikan tidak pulih selepas air diperbaiki" in the intro is stated as the general rule, but the facts show sources differ (Aquarium Co-Op recommends erythromycin directly); the guide later acknowledges the disagreement.
"Bakteria ini sememangnya ada dalam air atau lendir kulit ikan" merges two sources; acceptable.

"Jangkitan merebak ke badan, ada pendarahan atau tulang mula kelihatan" under 'Bila perlu risau' is the writer's own worry list, not a stated fact; similarly "Reput sudah menghampiri pangkal sirip" as a trigger to worry is inferred.
Table row "Garam dalam tangki (rutin)" with "Sumber tidak memberi jadual" presents salt as a treatment method; the facts only say routine salt is tolerated, not that it treats fin rot.
"Ikan yang dijangkiti patut dipindahkan ke tangki rawatan" is supported for columnaris only; fine.
"karbon atau media penjerap seumpamanya dikeluarkan": facts say carbon or Purigen; "media penjerap seumpamanya" is a generalisation of Purigen.
"ikan yang dijangkiti perlu dipindahkan ke tangki rawatan" for columnaris: the facts say hospital tank, which is close, but the guide ties it to fin rot in a way the facts don't state.

"ikan laga kerap terkena reput sirip kerana keadaan di kedai ikan hiasan tidak disokong oleh rujukan": the facts only say the claim lacks a citation (Wikipedia). The guide's wording is slightly loose.

"Kanamycin ... boleh dicampurkan ke dalam makanan ... ikut sukatan dan bahan campuran dalam arahan pengeluar": the facts give the mix of 1 scoop KanaPlex, 1 scoop Focus and 1 tbsp food, but the guide leaves it out. This is an omission, not an invented claim.
"Reput ... biasanya oleh bakteria" in the intro: broadly supported, but "biasanya" is a mild generalisation.
"Bakteria ini biasanya memang hidup di dalam air atau dalam lendir kulit ikan" merges two sources; acceptable but slightly blended.
"Asingkan ikan yang suka menggigit atau bergaduh" in step 2: the facts say remove nippers, so this is fine. The facts do not say to isolate fighting fish in this step.
"Pemakanan yang tidak baik dan makanan berlebihan" lists overfeeding as a predisposing factor. The facts name overfeeding as a stressor, so this is a minor generalisation.
"Ubat hanya digunakan jika ikan tidak pulih ... atau jika jangkitan semakin teruk" in the intro: the facts give no 'if the infection worsens' criterion.
"Pandangan sumber berbeza" is the guide's framing, not a fact. It is mild.

"Ubat ini juga boleh dicampur ke dalam makanan ... sehingga 1 minggu": the facts give the recipe (1 scoop KanaPlex, 1 scoop Focus, 1 tbsp food). The guide leaves out the Focus part, but nothing in it is invented.
"Bila perlu risau" bullet 'Reput sudah sampai ke pangkal sirip' as a worry trigger is the guide's own inference. The facts only say tissue cannot regrow.
"Jika mulut ikan turut reput, mungkin itu penyakit columnaris" is a mild extrapolation from the facts. The facts only say columnaris is highly contagious and fish should go to a hospital tank.
"Sumber yang sama mencadangkan suhu air 26–27 °C dan pH 7–8" says 'same source' about the second source (Mytour). This is correct, but 'sumber yang sama' reads ambiguously.

"Penternak menggunakan suplemen mineral untuk mengelakkannya" - the facts only name Wonder Shell/Seachem Equilibrium as skipped minerals. The guide generalizes without naming them, and the claim about what keepers do is slightly beyond the facts.
"Asingkan betina sebelum dia hampir bersalin" in the intro presents separation as a firm rule. The facts say sources differ, and one suggests a divider instead of moving her.

"Jika perut membengkak tetapi gravid spot tidak kelihatan, kemungkinan itu dropsy atau masalah pundi renang" - this is an inference. The facts only say the gravid spot is the key way to tell them apart, not that a missing spot means disease.
"Betina yang bunting juga sering mengejar jantan" is supported. The "Bila perlu risau" heading is the guide's own framing, and the facts don't say when to worry.
"Tangki kira-kira 38 liter": facts say about 10 gallons; the liter conversion is not in the facts (though it is roughly right).
"Jadi betina yang sudah diasingkan daripada jantan masih boleh bunting lagi": this is an inference the facts don't state.
"Jika kandungan lewat melebihi jangka biasa, periksa kualiti air": the facts only say poor water can delay birth. They don't give this advice for an overdue pregnancy.
"Pastikan keadaan airnya sama seperti tangki utama": the facts say this for the nursery tank. The guide moves it into the birthing setup, which is a minor shift.
"Gunakan penapis yang perlahan": the facts say 'gentle filtration'. The 'penapis span' example comes from the colony-breeding source.
"Jika perut besar dan tompok ... semakin gelap ... kemungkinan besar ikan itu bunting": this is a mild generalisation, but it is consistent with the facts.
"suplemen mineral untuk akuarium": the facts name Wonder Shell and Seachem Equilibrium. The guide generalises them, which is acceptable.
"Untuk ikan omnivor seperti ikan emas" in the intro is a small generalisation; the facts say peas suit omnivores but do not call goldfish omnivores.
"serangga air kecil" for the betta live food: the facts say "water bugs", which is close, but "daphnia (bo bo)" and the rest match. This is a minor loose translation.
"Kekalkan suhu air ikan emas di atas lebih kurang 70°F" is supported, but the earlier advice "Naikkan suhu secara perlahan" in the summary is only loosely backed.
"Ikan selalunya mengambil masa beberapa jam untuk pulih" is worded as general fish recovery. The facts tie this only to a shock-like presentation.
"jeli petroleum" for Vaseline is fine, but the guide gives no context for the advice beyond "bahagian badan yang terkeluar dari air".
"Antibiotik berasaskan kanamycin atau minocycline" – facts only name KanaPlex or Maracyn 2; the active ingredients are not in the facts.
"sisik menegak" – facts say "raised scales"; the wording is close, but "ikan emas/serangga air" detail is fine. Minor.
"Ikan selalunya pulih dalam beberapa jam" – facts say recovery from shock often takes a few hours; stated as a general outcome.

"(kira-kira 19 liter)" for 5 gallons and "kira-kira 26–27°C", "kira-kira 21°C", "5°C" – conversions not in facts (approximately correct, but added). The 5-gallon conversion is slightly off (about 19 L is right for US gallons).
"Biarkan air hanya beberapa sentimeter" – facts say a few inches; unit changed to centimetres, which understates the depth.
"kutu air" for daphnia (bo bo) and "serangga air" for water bugs – loose translations.
"Tempoh puasa... Sumber lain" and "Pastikan kitaran nitrogen tangki sudah lengkap" – paraphrase of "cycle the tank"; acceptable.
FAQ "kalau ramai ikan bertindak pelik, uji air dulu" – an inference not stated in the facts.

"Keracunan ammonia, nitrit atau nitrat... boleh membuatkan ikan berenang tidak terkawal" – facts only list ammonia as a nervous-system look-alike, and nitrate for goldfish. Nitrite is not stated to cause this.
"kira-kira 19 liter" for 5 gallons is a conversion not in the facts (arithmetically fine, but added).
"Langkah pertama... supaya ammonia dan nitrit kembali ke sifar" and "Selepas itu barulah pilih rawatan" is an ordering the facts do not state.
The intro says popeye is "akibat penyakit lain, kecederaan atau jangkitan"; this is a loose paraphrase of the facts.

"Rendaman garam untuk punca parasit ... Dalam tangki berasingan" merges the 1–3% bath with the separate-tank note. The facts list the separate tank for the formalin/salt/malachite green treatments, not for the bath specifically.
"Permukaan luar mata... Mata juga mungkin menunjukkan bintik putih atau merah" is fine, but the source for the bintik is a general fish description, not popeye-specific.
"Ikan emas dan cichlid besar ... menghasilkan banyak kotoran" is fine, but the guide says "popeye biasanya akibat penyakit... bukannya penyakit yang berdiri sendiri", which adds emphasis.

"Popeye pada kedua-dua mata lebih cenderung ke arah masalah kualiti air atau penyakit dalaman" - the facts do not say bilateral popeye points to water quality or internal disease. This is an invented diagnostic rule, repeated in the FAQ.

"Popeye pada sebelah mata sahaja mungkin berpunca daripada kecederaan" - the facts say injury may cause one-eye popeye. The guide extends this into a diagnostic rule and adds "digigit ikan lain" in the FAQ, which is slightly beyond the facts.
"Jika kedua-dua mata terkena, atau ikan juga berperut buncit... punca yang lebih mungkin ialah kualiti air atau penyakit dalaman seperti dropsy" - an unsupported inference.
"tuberkulosis ikan" and "penyakit buah pinggang" are slight embellishments. The facts say only "tuberculosis" and "kidney disease".
"Ichthyophthirius multifiliis (penyakit bintik putih)" - the white spot disease label is not in the facts.
"kerana itu tandanya masalah dalaman yang lebih serius" (dropsy) - not stated in the facts.
"Sebab itu ikan yang sakit perlu diasingkan" - an extra rationale that the facts do not state for this point.
"supaya ikan tidak panik dan melanggar dinding tangki" - the facts say only that the fish should not panic and crash. Reading it as hitting the tank walls is a minor addition.
"ikut label produk yang anda beli" is the writer's rule for undosed medicines; acceptable and not scored as a claim.
"Ikan keli dan ikan catfish lain": the facts only say catfish can be extremely sensitive to salt; naming ikan keli (Malaysian catfish) specifically is a small extension.
"yang biasa hidup dalam air keras, beralkali atau payau" is faithful to the facts.
"Buang telur yang tidak disenyawakan dan telur yang sudah diselaputi kulat" is supported.
"Rawat dengan segera": the facts say early diagnosis matters; the urgency framing is a mild generalisation.

"Kulat ini jarang menyerang ikan yang sihat" and the tank "nampak bersih" answer: attributing it to "suhu yang terlalu rendah" is supported in general terms, but "walaupun tangki nampak bersih" is the writer's framing.
"Jika jangkitan berulang... pastikan ikan tidak dirawat secara berlebihan" is a mild inference from the overtreatment fact.
"Penyakit kulat... biasa terdapat dalam air tawar dan air payau" is supported by source 1.

"Saprolegnia boleh tumbuh pada suhu 0–35 °C, tetapi paling suka suhu 15–30 °C": the facts give 32–95°F and 59–86°F. The guide's Celsius conversion is wrong. 32–95°F is 0–35°C and 59–86°F is 15–30°C, so it is roughly fine, but it is a writer's conversion.

"Pada masa yang sama, rawat kulatnya dengan garam atau ubat kulat": the intro recommends salt or antifungal as a general rule. The facts do not say this directly, and salt is not suitable for all fish.
"Potassium permanganate, formalin, larutan povidone iodine ... Ikut label produk yang dibeli": the facts give no dose, so 'by the label' is the writer's rule rather than a claim. This is acceptable.

"Celup garam (dip) ... bagi membuang parasit luaran ... 30 g/L": the Merck dip is for removing external parasites, not fungus. The guide says so but lists it as a fungus treatment option, which is a mild stretch.
"Jika ramai ikan terkena serentak ... mungkin itu columnaris atau ada masalah lain": the facts do not say that many affected fish indicates columnaris. This is an inference.
"Sebab itu bersihkan tangki dahulu": the facts do not say to clean the tank before treatment. This is a writer's addition.
"Jika ada carbon dalam penapis, keluarkan semasa rawatan": the facts only say carbon absorbs the medication. Removing it is a reasonable inference.
"Sebab itulah luka cetek ... boleh membawa maut" links the enzyme secretion to fatality; the facts do not state this causal link.
"Jangkitan yang berulang boleh berkait dengan rawatan berlebihan" is a slight stretch. The facts say overtreatment can lead to recurring infections, but this is presented as a reason for concern.
"Sesetengah sumber menegaskan" is vague. The facts attribute the claim to Practical Fishkeeping only.
"Columnaris dirawat dengan antibakteria seperti acriflavine" omits Terramycin. This is not an error.
"Kulat ini tidak boleh dihapuskan sepenuhnya" is supported.
"Dos berbeza mengikut sumber" and the table's "Satu sumber" labels are generalisations, but they are broadly consistent with the facts.
"Garam bukan beriodin" (non-iodised salt) is not in the facts.

"Saprolegnia boleh tumbuh pada 0–35 °C (32–95 °F) tetapi paling suka 15–30 °C": the Celsius conversions are not in the facts, which give only °F. The facts' 32–95°F is about 0–35°C and 59–86°F is about 15–30°C, so the numbers are right but the Celsius values are added.
"Walaupun begitu, kebanyakan penghobi tetap memanggilnya kulat": the claim about hobbyists is not in the facts.

"Cari punca asal seperti ... suhu terlalu rendah" and "Buang bahan organik yang mereput dan telur yang mati" are placed in the immediate-action list. The facts support them as causes and prevention, but not as first-aid steps.
"Perlu tutup penapis karbon semasa rawatan? Ya.": the facts say only that carbon removes medication. They do not say to switch it off, although this is a reasonable inference.

"Lebih membimbangkan lagi jika jangkitan berulang, kerana ia tanda punca asal belum diatasi atau rawatan diberi berlebihan": this interpretation of recurrence is partly invented. The facts link recurrence only to overtreatment.
"Pastikan dahulu ia bukan columnaris" and "atau ada tanda parasit luaran" as a reason to worry are framed as advice not found in the facts.
Table row 'Dalam makanan: 35–125 mg/kg' omits the fact that the dose is 35–125 mg/kg in food; this matches, but 'Sumber 3' attribution is fine. No issue.
'Rendaman dalam tangki' row: facts only say 'bath' (24 hours); 'dalam tangki' is a slight embellishment.
'membiak dengan cepat dalam sistem tertutup seperti akuarium': 'seperti akuarium' is an added example not in the facts.
'Sesetengah produk ubat cacing komersial dilaporkan boleh membahayakan siput': the facts say specifically 'Dactycid can harm snails'. Generalising to commercial products is a slight distortion.
'Kenal pasti kumpulannya kalau boleh': the facts say to work out which family is present, without the 'if possible' hedge. Minor.
'Satu sumber mengulang dos 2.5 mg/L pada hari ke-7 dan ke-14' and 'Penyelidik mencadangkan': minor rewording, supported.

'Ambil perhatian serius jika ikan ... mula mati' and the 'bila perlu risau' section are guide-framed advice assembled from the facts rather than stated in them. This is a small unsupported generality.
'Kurangkan makanan' in the immediate steps is not stated in the facts. The facts only say overfeeding raises ammonia.

Table: "Dalam makanan: 35–125 mg/kg selama sehingga 3 hari" is fine, but the intro claims "menyebabkan ikan ... insang membengkak" as a general sign; swelling is only in severe cases (minor generalisation).

"Kes yang berat boleh merebak dengan cepat dalam tangki, terutamanya pada suhu 22–25°C": the facts only say development is fast at that temperature; the claim about severe cases spreading is a stretch.
"Dapatkan bantuan doktor haiwan akuatik untuk pemeriksaan mikroskop dan preskripsi ubat": the vet is mentioned only for prescribing praziquantel in the US; this broader advice is not supported.
"Celup garam (garam tanpa iodin)": the facts do not mention iodine-free salt.
"hanya dalam tangki hospital yang beroksigen tinggi": the facts say well-aerated, not high-oxygen (minor).
"Praziquantel ... ubat pilihan utama ... Kalau cacing insang disahkan" in the intro: no problem, but "Ulang dos mengikut jadual" is generic.
FAQ: "keberkesanan celup garam berbeza mengikut spesies cacing": roughly supported by the Gyrodactylus data, but it is generalised.
"Satu produk ubat cacing insang komersial ... baca label dengan teliti": the facts only name Dactycid as harming snails; the advice to read the label is added.
"Bahan pengikat membantu" is supported. "Kajian ... masing-masing mengurangkan jangkitan lebih daripada 90 peratus" is supported.
"Sampel ... pernafasan makin laju" is supported. The vet advice and the label-reading advice are the main additions.
"Ikan perlu dikuarantin kerana punca dropsy mungkin berjangkit" is supported. The FAQ line "Kuarantin disarankan..." is also supported.
"(kira-kira 19–38 liter)" is a conversion the facts don't give. It is roughly correct, but it is an added number.
"(kira-kira 28–30 °C)" is a conversion the facts don't give. It is added, and 82–86°F is closer to 28–30°C, so it is acceptable but unsupported.
"(kira-kira 13 mg seliter)" is a conversion the facts don't give. It is added and unsupported.

"Pada dropsy ... selalunya ada tanda lain seperti mata tersembul, insang pucat atau ikan berhenti makan" is only loosely supported. The facts say tumours lack the other signs of disease, but they don't say "selalunya".
"Sumber-sumber tidak sama pendapat" and the claim that sources disagree on the chance of recovery are a framing the facts don't state. The underlying content is supported.
"Rawat air paip dengan penyahklorin" is supported. The 25–50% twice-weekly water change is attributed to a single source, which is acceptable.
"sirip terlipat rapat ke badan" is a rewording of "clamped fins" and is acceptable.
"Kuarantin paling berkesan jika penyakit dikesan awal" is supported.

"Peluang sembuh paling baik jika dikesan awal" in the intro is a generalisation. The facts only say some fish improve if treated early, and that quarantine works best when the illness is caught early.
"Uji air tangki (ammonia, nitrit, nitrat, pH)" lists specific parameters. The facts only say to test the water.
"ikan ditangkap atau dipindahkan" is a paraphrase of "handling". It is acceptable but loosely worded.
"Perhatikan ikan lain, terutamanya yang sama spesies" as a first-aid step is not stated in the facts.

"Kebanyakan sumber mengatakan ... prognosisnya buruk" and "sumber-sumber agak sepakat" are framing claims. They are roughly supported, but the FAQ line "Bagi ikan kecil ... sering disarankan" overstates the facts, which say the euthanasia advice comes from one source.
The intro says "selalunya kualiti air yang teruk dalam jangka masa panjang dan jangkitan bakteria". This is supported only loosely.
"Sebab itu ikan yang sakit perlu dikuarantin" in the FAQ is a reasonable inference, but it is not directly stated in that form.
"Menurut satu sumber... masing-masing boleh menyebabkan cecair terkumpul dalam rongga perut" is a paraphrase of ascites. It is fine.
"Sumber lain menyebut pemulihan tidak mungkin" is softened from "unlikely" to "not possible" ("tidak mungkin"), which is a slight overstatement.
"sisik menegak seperti pain" (pinecone scales) is in the facts only as a pinecone-scales emergency sign, but the guide's phrasing is acceptable; minor.
"Menaikkan suhu ke hujung atas julat yang sesuai untuk ikan laga" omits the 74-81°F range from the facts; generalised but not wrong.
"Menurut satu sumber veterinar, tiada rawatan untuknya" for Cryptobia is supported (Merck).
"Arowana ... secara semula jadi menjadi kurang aktif dan makan kurang": the facts say 'slow down and eat less', which is close enough.
"Jangan terlalu banyak" and "Selalunya beberapa cara ini perlu digabungkan" are supported.
"Jika ammonia atau nitrit melebihi sifar, tukar air dengan segera" in the intro omits the 30-50% figure and slightly turns a conditional recommendation into an urgent one; minor.
"Pea puffer dan scarlet badis ... memerlukan makanan hidup atau beku" is supported.
"Ikan juvenil ... anak ikan dan ikan juvenil yang tidak makan lebih daripada 24 jam" is supported as an emergency.
"Sembelit ... Jika dibiarkan, sembelit boleh menyebabkan masalah pundi renang" is supported.
"Ikan dewasa sudah melepasi tempoh puasa selamat untuk jenisnya" as a worry trigger is an inference not directly stated in the facts.
"kira-kira 23–27 °C" is an invented Celsius conversion of 74–81°F. The facts give no Celsius figure, and 74–81°F is about 23–27°C.
"Sembelit" is presented as a general treatment. The facts only say that fasting for 24–48 hours can clear constipation. They do not link this to a fish that refuses food.

"Guna blok makanan" is listed as a common mistake. The facts only say that food blocks can leave uneaten food rotting and that many species do not recognise them, so this is a mild over-generalisation.

"Ikan laga baru yang stres ... Ya, ikan baru yang stres ..." and "Beri makanan lama bersama makanan baru" in the FAQ for betta pellets applies the old-with-new advice to this case. The facts give that advice for switching foods in general, so this is a small extension.

"Air yang lebih panas pula meningkatkan metabolisme" and the other general statements are supported. "Patutkah saya terus tukar air..." combines facts about old tank syndrome and water changes. The FAQ answer is a plausible synthesis, but it presents "selalunya melebihi 10 mg/L" as the trigger for avoiding water changes, which the facts do not exactly say.
"Insang dan darah bertukar warna coklat gelap seperti coklat" - facts say chocolate-brown; minor wording, fine.
"(lebih kurang 0.95 liter)" - the litre conversion for one quart is not in the facts (small added detail, correct but unsupported).
"Ikan keli saluran" for channel catfish - translation addition, harmless.

"Kedua-dua keadaan ini memerlukan ikan dipindahkan, bukan sekadar tukar air" - the facts give this for old tank syndrome and for ammonia >5 mg/L with pH <7, but the 'not just water change' wording for the second condition is an extrapolation.
"Ikan yang keracunan nitrit ... Ikan berkumpul dekat saluran udara" listed as a worry sign - fine.
"pemanas cepat menghabiskan bateri" - facts say it drains the battery; 'cepat' is a small embellishment.
"Pertimbangkan diagnosis makmal ... Punca tidak dapat dikenal pasti" - 'when to worry more' advice is not in the facts, but is a reasonable generality.
"Ikan yang hampir mati ... patut dimatikan" - supported.
"tidak lebih daripada kira-kira 0.5 °C sejam" contradicts the facts: the limit is 1°F (about 1°C) per hour.
"kira-kira 1 liter air tangki" is a conversion/change: the facts say about one quart (roughly 0.95 L), so it is approximately fine but not exact.
"Insang dan darah bertukar warna coklat seperti coklat masakan" is a odd rewording of chocolate-brown; minor.
"Ikan keli saluran" etc. is supported; "Kalau pH naik lebih daripada 1 unit" is supported.
"kerana paras oksigen paling rendah pada waktu pagi" is supported.
"Pam udara berbateri" is supported.
"Kematian berterusan walaupun parameter air sudah baik" in the worry section is not in the facts (invented trigger).
"pH jatuh di bawah 6.0 dalam tangki yang lama tidak dibuang airnya" is supported only loosely.
The opening line "kuatkan pengudaraan ... uji air" as the first step is a general recommendation not directly in the facts.
"Bagi ikan yang sudah tidak mahu makan, rendaman dalam air ialah pilihan" – the facts do not say this; it is the writer's inference.

"Rendaman dengan suhu tinggi ... 1 tablet metronidazole setiap 20 liter" – the facts say 1 tablet of Metronidazol per 20 litres, but the table lists it as 'Rendaman dengan suhu tinggi'. This is only loosely supported.
"Nasihat ini tidak sesuai dengan kaedah makanan berubat, jadi ikut satu kaedah sahaja" – the facts do not say this. It is the writer's rule.
"Sumber lain menyebut nama yang berbeza" and the idea that the sources describe different names – an editorial framing the facts do not state.

"Metronidazole ... disebut oleh sumber-sumber untuk Hexamita. Ia hanya untuk ikan yang bukan untuk dimakan" – the facts limit the 'non-food fish' remark to Spironucleus. The guide applies it to Hexamita generally.

"Kalau ikan menolak makanan lebih daripada tiga hari ... asingkan ikan dan mulakan rawatan metronidazole dengan segera" – the facts only say to treat at once. They do not name the drug here, and the guide adds isolation to this trigger.
"jadi rupa luaran sahaja tidak cukup untuk menilai tahap jangkitan" – the writer's inference. The facts only say that heavily infected fish often showed no other abnormalities.
"Menurut sumbernya, Spironucleus menyerang semua jenis cichlid, ikan laga..." – this is fine. 'Ikan laga' for betta is a translation, not an unsupported claim.
"produk ubat siap guna yang seumpamanya (ikut label produk itu)" – the facts name API General Cure with no dose. 'By the label' is the writer's rule, not a claim.

"Warna menjadi gelap" and "berlegar dekat permukaan air" are listed under later signs in discus, but the facts give darkened colour and hovering near the surface as general signs (source 2), not later-stage ones. This is a small reassignment.

"Ikan berbaring dekat dasar tangki ... kadang-kadang ada luka di perut" is fine. But "Lubang kecil ... Kes teruk" puts head pits under severe cases, and the facts do not say they are severe-stage signs.
"Penyakit ini menyerang semua jenis cichlid, ikan laga, gourami" is attributed to Hexamita/the disease in general, but the facts say this only for Spironucleus.

"Discus, oscar dan angelfish dikatakan paling mudah dijangkiti" is supported. However, the opening that Hexamita is "juga dipanggil Spironucleus" is not stated in the facts. They treat the two as separate names and never say they are the same organism.

Step 1 and the intro say to treat with metronidazole in a quarantine tank at 28–30 °C. This sits awkwardly with the later 32–33 °C or 86–88 °F advice, and it presents a mix of rules from different sources as one procedure.

"Dubur bengkak dan merah, kadang-kadang ada luka di perut" matches the facts. "Anak ikan dan ikan muda mula mati" under "Bila perlu risau" is an added worry trigger, since the facts only list it as a Spironucleus sign.

"Seorang moderator forum mendapati metronidazole sahaja mungkin tidak melekat dengan baik" omits the fact's other half, that the moderator also used a product like API General Cure. This is a minor omission.

"Mandian | Metronidazole 5 mg/L | 3 jam sehari selama 5 hari" and the food row combine facts correctly, but the merged food row 'Metronidazole 50 mg/kg ... 5 hari berturut-turut' is a blend of sources; acceptable but slightly interpreted.
"Ikan baharu yang baru sampai: jangkitan ... boleh menyebabkan kematian dalam masa seminggu" is generalised from the angelfish shipping finding to any new fish.
"Najis putih berlendir pada ikan discus, angelfish dan cichlid lain sering dikaitkan dengan Hexamita" is a mild generalisation.
"Ikan saya nampak sihat... Ya" is a FAQ answer that goes a little beyond the facts.
"kepala dan perut yang cengkung" is acceptable for 'sunken head and belly'.
"Bolehkah metronidazole digunakan dalam tangki yang ada udang atau siput? Tidak digalakkan" is the writer's inference from the toxicity fact; acceptable.
The intro sentence 'rawatan dengan metronidazole mengikut dos dan jadual yang betul' is a mild generality, not a claim.

"1 g bagi setiap kira-kira 76 liter": facts say 1 gram per 20 gallons; the litre conversion is the writer's and the guide omits the original unit (~75.7 L is arithmetically fine, but presented as source figure).
"suhu dinaikkan ke kira-kira 30–31 °C": facts say 86 to 88 (Fahrenheit implied), i.e. about 30–31 °C. The conversion is correct but the Fahrenheit unit was only implied in the facts.
"suhu kira-kira 35.5 °C selama lima hari": facts say 96°F, which is about 35.5 °C. The conversion is right, but it is the writer's own figure.
"Warna badan menjadi gelap" is listed under later signs: the facts list darkened colour among the general signs, not as a later stage.
"kadang-kadang berjuntai dari badan": the facts do not say the feces trail or hang from the body. They say 'mucus-trailing' and 'stringy'.

"Cara pasti untuk mengesahkan Hexamita ialah pemeriksaan wet mount di bawah mikroskop" and "Hexamita hanya dapat disahkan melalui pemeriksaan wet mount": the facts only say diagnosis is made with a wet mount (for Spironucleus). They do not say it is the only sure way or that a microscope is needed.
"menggunakan produk ubat lain mengikut label": the facts only say the moderator used a product like API General Cure. No label dosing is given for it.
"1 biji tablet metronidazole bagi setiap 20 liter ... Suhu 32–33 °C" is credited to "Penternak discus", but the facts call it a Vietnamese method.
"Ini berbeza dengan kaedah makanan berubat yang memerlukan ikan makan": the writer's own comparison, not stated in the facts.
Title and intro frame the guide as discus-only, while the topic is angelfish. Several angelfish findings are mixed in without clear separation.
"Metronidazole ialah ubat yang paling kerap disebut" is a mild unsupported generalisation; the facts only list it as the treatment.
"Pilih satu kaedah sahaja dan ikut dengan tepat" is advice not stated in the facts, though it is consistent with the warnings against overdosing.

"kepala dan perut yang kelihatan cengkung" is acceptable (sunken head and belly), but the "Rawat jika ikan enggan makan lebih daripada tiga hari" step is placed under first aid without a source ordering. This is minor.
"Metronidazole disenaraikan ... hanya untuk ikan yang bukan ikan makanan" is supported.
The table labels the 1 g per 20 gallons dose as "Dalam tangki" and the Vietnamese method as "Rendaman". The "rendaman" label for the Vietnamese method is an interpretation of "2-day soak".
"lebih kurang 75 liter" for 20 gallons is an added conversion not in the facts (roughly correct).
"lebih kurang 30–31 °C" and "lebih kurang 35.5 °C" are conversions not in the facts. The facts only imply Fahrenheit for 86–88.
"Hexamita memang punca yang paling terkenal" is supported, but "selalunya dikaitkan dengan Hexamita" in the intro is a mild generalisation.
"Perut membengkak; dalam kes lain kepala dan perut kelihatan cengkung" merges separate keeper accounts. It is acceptable but loosely framed.

"Seorang penternak mencadangkan makanan berubat untuk dua atau tiga kali pemberian setiap tiga bulan" is supported. "Penternak berpengalaman" as the source label for the 1 g/20 gal dose is not in the facts.
"rawat dalam tangki berasingan" in the shrimp/snail FAQ answer is an inference. The facts only say metronidazole is toxic to shrimp and snails.
"Jangkitan pada ikan yang baru dihantar boleh membawa maut dalam masa seminggu" generalises the angelfish shipping finding to discus.
The moderator's "digantikan dengan ubat campuran untuk parasit dalaman" paraphrases API General Cure with extra description.
"กลับมาแล้วให้เปลี่ยนน้ำ 25–50%": the facts say to change 25–50% if you are away from home during the outage. They don't say to do it after returning. This is a small added detail.
"ย้ายปลาไปตู้หรือบ่ออื่นเร็วเกินไป": the facts call moving fish a last resort. They don't say it is wrong only when done too early. This is a minor reframing.
"ใช้ตามฉลากของผลิตภัณฑ์" (oxygen tablets): the facts give no dose, so this is the writer's rule rather than a claim. It is minor.

"ปลาน่าจะผ่านคืนไปได้" and "ไม่ถึง 2 ชั่วโมงปลาอยู่ได้โดยไม่มีกรอง": the facts say short outages are generally fine and fish should make it overnight if aeration or circulation is provided. The guide's wording is close but slightly merged.
"ผู้ค้าปลารายหนึ่ง": the facts say a Sri Lankan trade source. This is slightly generalized but acceptable.
"ถ้าไฟดับนานเกินหนึ่งสัปดาห์ ให้ขอร้านปลา...ฝากเลี้ยง": supported by the facts.
"ปิดห้องไว้" at 4–8 hours: supported by the facts. The facts do not explain why.
"ซื้อปั๊มลมแบบชาร์จได้หรือแบบใส่ถ่าน": supported. The guide leaves out the Hailea CP-60 example, which is fine.
"ปริมาณให้ใช้ตามฉลากของผลิตภัณฑ์ที่ซื้อ" (oxygen tablets: follow the label) is not in the facts.
"ปลาน่าจะผ่านคืนไปได้" is a softened version of the fact: fish should make it overnight if aeration or circulation is provided. The guide drops the condition in the table context.
"ตรวจว่าฮีตเตอร์ทำงานปกติ" is a loose rendering of the fact that says check the heaters.
The temperature section's "กันความร้อนออก (อากาศเย็น)" and the "ปิดห้องไว้" row are interpretive additions. The facts only say keep the room closed, with no stated reason.
"ปลาคาร์ป" for koi is a translation shift. The facts say koi.
"ผู้เลี้ยงหลายคนเล่าว่า" (many keepers) is slightly overstated. The facts say only that keepers report it.
"ถ้าไฟดับนาน ... ในระบบกรอง" is attributed to a canister filter, but the facts say this about filters in general during a long outage.
"ถ้าไม่อยู่บ้านตอนไฟดับ เมื่อกลับมาให้เปลี่ยนน้ำ" adds "on return" timing that is not in the facts.

"ฮีตเตอร์ 10 วัตต์กินไฟน้อยกว่าแบบ 100 วัตต์มาก" is supported, but the FAQ line "ถ้าจำเป็นต้องใช้ไฟสำรองกับฮีตเตอร์ ให้เลือกตัวที่วัตต์ต่ำ" is a recommendation not in the facts, which only say not to run the heater from a UPS.
"ควรใช้ UPS กับระบบกรองแทน" in the FAQ is an inference; the facts only say a UPS can run the filter.
"ปลาส่วนใหญ่อดอาหารได้อย่างน้อยราวหนึ่งสัปดาห์" is stronger than the facts, which say days to weeks or about a week.
"อีกวิธีที่มีแหล่งแนะนำคือล้างวัสดุกรองด้วยน้ำจากตู้ แล้ววางกลับไว้ในตู้" is supported but sits in tension with the sponge advice. It is a minor merge of two sources.
"ปิดห้องไว้" and "ปิดฝาตู้ แล้วห่อตู้ด้วย... ผ้าห่ม ถุงนอน หนังสือพิมพ์" are acceptable. However, "เติมน้ำใหม่ให้เต็มกรองก่อน" adds "full" where the facts only say to prime with new water.
"ตู้ที่ปล่อยปลาน้อยกว่า ... แอมโมเนียจะขึ้นช้ากว่า" is supported. "ช่วงอากาศร้อนจึงต้องระวังเป็นพิเศษ" is a mild unsupported generalization.

The guide's opening says to pour water or use a battery pump "ก่อนที่ปลาจะเริ่มลอยหัว", which is fine. However, "ไฮโดรเจนซัลไฟด์สะสมอยู่" in the canister FAQ is slightly generalized from the filter in general to canisters.
"ลูกปลาและปลาแก้ว มีอัตราการตายสูง": the facts say very young and very old fish die at high rates. Ambassis (glass fish) is only named in the copper toxicity data, so this is a mix-up.
"ปลาที่ป่วยหนักส่วนใหญ่ตายเพราะขาดอากาศ": the facts say death is usually from suffocation, so this is roughly fine. "ส่วนใหญ่" for severely ill fish is a slight overstatement.
"เพราะยาจะฆ่าได้เฉพาะระยะที่ว่ายอยู่อิสระในน้ำเท่านั้น" is given as the reason to treat both tanks. The facts give a different reason for that: the disease spreads easily.

"ลอยหัวฮุบอากาศ" is listed as a sign of fish crowding near the surface. The facts say sick fish stay near the surface gasping, so this is fine. Using it as a flat sign of heavily infected gills is a small extrapolation.
"ให้ใช้ตามฉลากของผลิตภัณฑ์ที่ซื้อ" for aquarium salt and for the other medicines is the writer's rule rather than a claim from the facts, so it is acceptable.

"ปลาที่เล็กมากและแก่มากจะตายจากโรคนี้มากเป็นพิเศษ" and the claim that the crucian carp is "ปลาไนเงิน" are fine. The "คอปเปอร์ซัลเฟต (แช่)" row and the "คอปเปอร์คีเลตผสมเอง" row's note on Amyloodinium follow the facts.
"ยังไม่มีงานวิจัยยืนยัน" (about the Aquarium Co-op salt-plus-darkness method): the facts only call it anecdotal. They don't say that no research confirms it.

"ควรแยกปลาป่วยไปรักษาในตู้แยก" (in the shrimp and snail copper answer): the facts say to isolate sick fish but to treat both tanks. They don't advise a separate-tank copper treatment to protect shrimp and snails, so this is a mild extrapolation.
"ควรให้ยาต่อเนื่องอย่างน้อยราวหนึ่งสัปดาห์": the facts say to treat for about a week, not "at least" a week. This is a minor wording drift.
"หรือจะแยกปลาป่วยไปรักษาในตู้พยาบาลก็ได้" in the shrimp/snail FAQ: the facts only say remove invertebrates or use medicated food; a hospital tank for this case is not stated.
"ใช้ยาแบบผสมอาหารตามฉลากแทน": fine, but the FAQ ties it to a hospital tank option that the facts do not support.

"Gentian violet ... ตามฉลากผลิตภัณฑ์" and "Malachite green ... ตามฉลากผลิตภัณฑ์": the facts give no dose or label guidance for these, and the guide adds a label rule. This is the writer's rule rather than a fact, and mildly risky.
"ยาปฏิชีวนะในตู้พยาบาล ... รักษาในตู้แยก": the facts say only 'antibiotics in a treatment tank'. This is a small extension.
"แหล่งที่แนะนำไม่ได้ระบุระยะเวลา" for erythromycin and methylene blue: this is the writer's commentary. It is harmless but not from the facts.
"ควรกังวลเมื่อ ... แผลมีเลือดออก": the facts list bleeding only in advanced cases. The 'when to worry' section is partly the writer's own synthesis.
"ถ้าดูแลน้ำมาหลายวันแล้วยังไม่ดีขึ้นจึงค่อยพิจารณาใช้ยา" in the intro: this is a Mytour recommendation stated as a general rule. It does not conflict with the facts.

"ใช้เกลือรักษาครีบเปื่อยได้ ... เกลือ 1–3 กรัม/ลิตร" and the table row "เกลือแช่ในตู้ตามปกติ" present the routine-salt figure as a fin-rot treatment. The facts give 1–3 g/L only as routine salt that most tropical fish tolerate. They give no salt dose for treating fin rot.
"เอาคาร์บอนหรือเรซินดูดซับออก": the facts say to remove carbon or Purigen. Calling Purigen a generic "resin adsorbent" is a small paraphrase beyond the facts.
"ได้รับบาดเจ็บบ่อยกว่าปลาอื่น": the facts say long, delicate fins are awkward to use and get injured often. They make no comparison with other fish.
The salt FAQ answer says salt works "ช้ากว่ายา". The facts say this only about salt compared with erythromycin, not compared with medicines in general.

The source labels in the treatment table are inconsistent. Malachite green and the long-term salt bath come from source 0 but are labelled "แหล่งที่ 1". The 1–3 g/L aquarium salt is from source 2 but is labelled "แหล่งที่ 2". The 3 ppt salt figure is from source 3 and is labelled "แหล่งที่ 3". This is a small attribution slip, not an invented claim.

The 30 g/L salt dip is placed in the antifungal treatment table. The facts give it only for removing external parasites. The guide does say this, but putting it there could suggest it is a fungal treatment.
The advice to use the other medicines "ตามฉลากของผลิตภัณฑ์" is the writer's own rule. The facts give no doses for those medicines, so this is not a factual claim.
"ใช้เกลือที่ไม่มีไอโอดีน" (non-iodised salt) – not in the facts; invented note.
"oxytetracycline" – facts name Terramycin, not oxytetracycline (brand/generic equivalence is the writer's addition).
"ควรทำความสะอาดตู้ก่อนเริ่มรักษา" – facts only say chemicals react with organic matter; the cleaning-before-treatment advice is not stated.
"ถ้ารักษาในตู้ให้ถอดคาร์บอนออกก่อน" – facts say carbon absorbs treatment and to treat eggs separately; removing carbon is a reasonable inference but not directly stated.
"เปลี่ยนน้ำสม่ำเสมอ" (regular water changes) – not in facts.
"ปลาหนัง" for catfish and "ปลาป่วยหลายตัวพร้อมกัน ... ควรตรวจ" – the multiple-fish worry section is the writer's extrapolation from 'typically only one fish'.
"ราขึ้นที่เหงือก" as a trigger to worry – extrapolated from the general fatal-if-untreated statement.
Claim that microscopy helps tell columnaris from Saprolegnia – facts only describe hyphae under microscope, not as a differentiator.
"ราไม่มีทางหมดไปจากระบบได้ทั้งหมด" is supported, but "ถอดคาร์บอนออกตอนใส่ยา" in FAQ is stated as a firm instruction rather than a fact-backed one.
"แพะ (corydoras)" - corydoras is rendered oddly as 'แพะ' (goat); a translation error, not in the facts.
"อาหารแช่แข็งแบบก้อนเหมาะกับการฝากคนมาให้มากกว่า" - the facts only say frozen cubes are cleaner and easier to portion for sitters; the comparison 'more suitable' is a mild generalisation.
"บอกไว้ว่าถ้าวันไหนมาไม่ได้ ให้ข้ามมื้อนั้นไปเลย" - the facts say to skip a missed day; the guide frames it as an instruction to the sitter, which is a reasonable reading.
"ตรวจให้แน่ใจว่าเปิดระบบกรองกลับแล้ว" is placed as a preparation step; the facts list it only as a common mistake, which is a minor reframing.
"ซึ่งทำให้ปลาตายมากกว่าการอดอาหารไปบางมื้อ" - this is supported by one source, but the guide states it in the intro as a general fact.
"ถ้าเลี้ยงปลาที่เลือกกิน หรือต้องไปนานกว่า 1 สัปดาห์" - supported by the facts (picky eaters or trips over a week).
"หนอนแดง ไรทะเล" – frozen food examples (bloodworms, brine shrimp) are not in the facts; the facts only say frozen cubes are cleaner and easier to portion.
"ไรแดง" for daphnia – a loose translation; daphnia is a water flea, not exactly 'ไรแดง'. This is a minor wording issue.
"ควรมีคนแวะมาดูเครื่องทุก 2–3 วัน" – the facts say 'check every few days' for the feeder. The 2–3 day interval is specific to sitter visits, so this is a slight specification.

"ถ้าไม่อยู่นานกว่า 1 สัปดาห์ก็ไม่ควรปล่อยให้อดเช่นกัน" is placed right after the large/carnivorous/older fish sentence. The facts do support it as a general rule, so the placement is slightly misleading.
"ภายใน 2–3 วันหลังกลับมา" – the facts say 'within a few days'. The 2–3 figure is a slight specification.
"ที่ทำให้ปลาตายบ่อยที่สุดคือการให้อาหารมากเกินไป" – the facts say overfeeding by helpers kills more fish than missed meals. The intro generalises this to all overfeeding.
"ควรเผื่อเวลาปรับจำนวนรูให้ลงตัว" (allow time to adjust the number of holes) is advice not in the facts.
"ส่วนสิ่งสำคัญคือทำให้น้ำกระจายทั่ววัสดุกรองอย่างสม่ำเสมอ" is a mild generalisation. The facts only say an even trickle is hard.
"ได้รับอากาศดีมาก" (very well aerated) slightly overstates the facts, which say "well aerated".
"เมื่อไฟกลับมาแล้วให้ตรวจดูว่าปั๊มทำงานต่อจริง" narrows the facts. They say to check that the filter restarted, not specifically the pump.
"เพราะปั๊มไม่ต้องดันน้ำขึ้นสูงมาก" – the facts only say one keeper argues it loses less flow to pump head; this reason is invented, and it is also odd because a top-mounted unit pumps water up.
"ถ้าไฟดับ ให้เปิดปั๊มลมแบบใช้แบตเตอรี่ทันที" – the facts only say a battery air pump keeps fish supplied with oxygen; "immediately" is an added instruction.
"จึงควรค่อย ๆ ปรับไป" – the advice to adjust gradually is not in the facts.
"ตามวงจรไนโตรเจน" – the nitrogen cycle is not named in the facts.
"ซัมพ์ที่ใช้ K1 แบบเคลื่อนที่" – the facts say a fluidised-bed K1 sump; this is acceptable but slightly reworded.
"ให้ใส่ไว้ในลิ้นชักที่อยู่ต่อจากใยกรอง" and "ชั้นแรกเป็นกรองกล ตามแบบที่ใช้กันทั่วไป" – these mix two different keepers' designs into one prescriptive installation procedure.
"ส่วนการปล่อยน้ำออกทางสเปรย์บาร์ใกล้ผิวน้ำน่าจะช่วยให้เงียบลง" – the facts only say one keeper expected the spray bar to be quiet; the guide presents this as a general likelihood.
"ระหว่างนี้ให้ย้ายวัสดุกรองชีวภาพ... ตรงเหนือหัวทรายของปั๊มลมแบตเตอรี่" – this is roughly supported, but the facts say the media goes above the airstone, not specifically the battery pump's airstone.
"ถ้าสาหร่ายหนาแน่นมากและการให้อากาศอ่อน" is supported, but "ปลาลอยอยู่ใต้ผิวน้ำ... แสดงว่าออกซิเจนอาจต่ำ" is slightly extended from the facts (minor).
"ผู้เพาะพันธุ์บางคนจึงตั้งใจทำน้ำเขียว" adds the causal "therefore", which the facts do not state (minor).
"แหล่งข้อมูลหนึ่งยังระบุการใส่ปุ๋ยน้ำว่าเป็นสาเหตุหนึ่งด้วย" is supported only loosely by the facts (minor).
"ไม้น้ำจะทรุดโทรม" slightly overstates "hard on plants" (minor).
"หรือใช้ปุ๋ยน้ำอยู่แล้ว" – the facts list liquid fertilizer as a cause, but the guide's wording is a loose addition and is weakly supported.

"จุดนี้ใช้แยกน้ำเขียวออกจากตะไคร่ที่เกาะตามพื้นผิว" – the facts say algae float rather than grow on glass. They don't say this distinguishes green water from other algae, so this is an added inference.
"ให้เพิ่มการให้อากาศทันที" – the facts have no instruction to increase aeration immediately. They only say to keep aeration running.

"น้ำที่เคยเขียวเข้มเปลี่ยนเป็นดำ เทา น้ำตาล หรือใสขึ้นมาเอง แสดงว่าสาหร่ายอาจตายลงจำนวนมาก ... แอมโมเนียอาจพุ่งขึ้น" – this reading is an inference. The facts say the colour change follows a die-off, and say nothing about 'on its own' or about an ammonia warning in this context.

"สาเหตุที่น่าจะพบบ่อยที่สุดคือแร่ธาตุหรือธาตุอาหารในน้ำหมด" – the facts give this as the likely reason a large bloom dies back. The guide places it in the immediate-action section with loose framing, and 'prepare for it' is not a stated recommendation.
"แล้วการเปลี่ยนน้ำตามปกติจะทำให้น้ำใสขึ้น" is supported. "ตู้โชว์" (display tank) in the FAQ is not in the facts, which only say green water hides the view.
The intro says "ออกซิเจนต้องสูง" (oxygen must be high) for arowana in general. The facts give the high dissolved oxygen need only for Asian arowana. This is a small generalisation.

"เพื่อลดโอกาสเกิดโรคและอาการตาตก" (to reduce the chance of disease and drop eye) implies that temperature control, water changes and diet prevent drop eye. The facts give no proven cause or prevention for drop eye beyond tank size and fewer collisions, so this is a mild overreach.
"ใช้คอปเปอร์ซัลเฟตตามฉลาก" / "ใช้ควินินตามฉลาก" / "ยาและเกลือให้ใช้ตามฉลาก": label dosing for products with no dose in the facts is the writer's rule (acceptable per instructions, minor)
"เปลี่ยนน้ำ 1/4 ทุก 3 วัน" for cloudy eye: roughly matches 'every third day' but fine

"ผู้เลี้ยงหลายคนบอกว่าเห็บปลาและหนอนสมอส่วนใหญ่มากับอาหารมีชีวิต" is placed in the feeder-fish mistakes section, tying it to livebearers/goldfish; facts only say live feeder foods generally (slight generalization)
"ปลาโตเต็มวัยวันละครั้ง ปลาเล็กวันละ 2–3 ครั้ง" is supported; "ผู้เลี้ยงบางรายเห็นว่าตาตกไม่ใช่โรค" is supported (one keeper)

"ควรให้กุ้ง หอยแมลงภู่ เนื้อปลา ไส้เดือนดิน หรือแมลงอย่างจิ้งหรีดแทน": the FAQ recommendation of alternatives is a synthesis from separate facts (crickets listed only for adult silver arowanas), a minor generalization
"ฟาร์มบางแห่งย้ายปลาไปเลี้ยงในบ่อกลางแจ้ง": facts say breeders move fish to outdoor ponds; fine
Intro "ก่อนซื้อให้เตรียมตู้ ... ให้อาหารที่ผิวน้ำ" and "จึงต้องใช้ตู้ใหญ่" are general statements loosely supported
"ถ้าเห็นอาการผิดปกติ ... ให้ดูคุณภาพน้ำและอุณหภูมิเป็นอย่างแรก": the facts give no such general first-step rule. It is the writer's own advice.
"ตอนเช้าให้เปิดไฟในห้องก่อน": the facts say to light the room gradually before the tank lights. They don't limit this to the morning.
"ปลาเอาตัวถูกับวัสดุในตู้ (flashing)": the facts only list "flashing" as a sign. The guide's description of it is the writer's gloss.
"ระบบกรองต้องแรง" and "ตู้ปลาจึงต้องกว้างและยาว" in the intro are loose generalisations beyond the stated figures.
"ปลาอะโรวาน่าตัวโตเต็มที่ยาวได้ราว 90 ซม." in the intro generalises; the facts also give 120 cm for wild silvers and 900 mm for Asian.

"แต่ทุกแหล่งเห็นตรงกันว่าอะโรวาน่าขับถ่ายมาก ต้องเปลี่ยนน้ำ...และไม่ควรเปลี่ยนน้ำทั้งหมดในครั้งเดียว" says all sources agree; the facts give the waste point to one source and the no-full-change point to another.
"ควรเลือกกุ้ง หอยแมลงภู่ ไส้เดือน เนื้อปลา และแมลงอย่างจิ้งหรีดแทน" in the FAQ: this is a recommendation built from the facts, not stated in them.
"ให้อาหารที่หลากหลายทางผิวน้ำ" in the intro: surface feeding and variety are loosely implied, but the facts do not say variety is required.
"ถ้าตาเริ่มตก ให้ลงมือแต่เนิ่น ๆ ... ให้เน้นลดการชนและทบทวนเรื่องการให้อาหาร": the facts give no action for fish that have already begun to show drop eye; this is the writer's own advice.
"ถ้าปลาไม่กินอาหารนานเกิน 1 วัน ... ให้ตรวจคุณภาพน้ำก่อน แล้วสังเกตอาการให้ละเอียด": the facts name this as a warning sign but give no action.

"จึงต้องใช้ตามฉลากของผลิตภัณฑ์ที่ซื้อมา" for salt, copper sulfate and quinine: the facts give no doses, so this is a writer's rule. It is allowed here, but the guide stretches it to quinine and copper sulfate treatments that are risky.
"ปลาที่เลี้ยงในบ่อแทบไม่เป็นตาตก" is slightly overstated; the facts say only that drop eye is rarely seen in ponds.
No invented dose, medicine or cause found. Every number, product and recommendation traces to the facts.
Minor: the guide puts the Dimilin 25W aquarium-outbreak dose in the table as one case. It is labelled that way, so this is fine.
Minor: 'ผลิตภัณฑ์ไดฟลูเบนซูรอนหรือลูเฟนูรอนอื่นๆ ... ตามฉลาก' is the writer's rule, not a claim from the facts.
"ให้ใช้เกลือที่ไม่มีไอโอดีน" (use non-iodized salt): the facts never say this.
"ให้วิตามินซีและจุลินทรีย์ช่วยย่อย" (vitamin C and digestive microbes): the facts say vitamin C and digestive enzymes (men tiêu hóa), not microbes or probiotics.
The intro says to start treatment on seeing even one parasite, for both Lernaea and Argulus. The facts give that rule only for Argulus.
"ระหว่างนั้นมันยังดูดเลือด" (it keeps sucking blood meanwhile): the facts say only that it keeps feeding (hút) and releasing eggs. Blood is not mentioned.
"ไรแดง" is used for Daphnia, but the facts say bo bo (Daphnia). Daphnia is usually a water flea, and ไรแดง is also the Thai name for it, so this is a minor translation point.
"ใบเลี่ยน (Melia azedarach)": the facts say only "lá xoan". The Latin species name is added without support.
"ใช้ตามฉลากของผลิตภัณฑ์ที่ซื้อ" for diflubenzuron/lufenuron and trichlorfon: the facts give no dose, so this is the writer's own rule. It is allowed.
"การใช้เกินขนาดเป็นความผิดพลาดที่พบบ่อย" for potassium permanganate: this is supported by the mistakes section.
"เห็บปลาเป็นแผ่นกลมแบน" in the how-to-tell section: the facts say a flat disc (đĩa dẹt), but "round" is added. This is minor.

"ปลาที่เพิ่งปล่อยลงตู้มาหลายสัปดาห์แล้วก็อาจเป็นต้นทางได้": the barramundi case was an aquarium outbreak and is reasonably generalised. The reply to "ไม่ได้ซื้อปลาใหม่เลย" contradicts the premise and goes beyond the facts.
"ให้วิตามินซีกับจุลินทรีย์ช่วยย่อย": the facts say digestive enzymes (men tiêu hóa), not microbes/probiotics. This turns the fact around.
"แหล่งหนึ่งแนะนำให้เริ่มจากเพิ่มความเค็มก่อน" is supported. "ถ้าปลาตัวโตพอ ... ทาแผลทันที" is supported.
The intro summary line says "เพราะตัวอ่อนและไข่ที่อยู่ในน้ำ" and the table says "ฆ่าสัตว์จำพวกกุ้งกั้งปู" for diflubenzuron. Both are consistent with the facts.
"ตัวเต็มวัยอยู่ได้หลายวันโดยไม่ต้องมีปลา" and similar details are supported.

"ผลิตภัณฑ์ diflubenzuron สำหรับบ่อปลา": the facts name NT Labs Argusol and give 10 ml per 364 L. They don't say it is for ponds. The guide also says to dose "ตามฉลาก", which is the writer's rule, not a fact.
"หนอนเกาะที่ปากหรือเหงือก จนปลากินอาหารไม่ได้": the facts link feeding failure only to worms on the mouth. They don't link it to worms on the gills.
"แผลบวมแดง เป็นแผลเปื่อย" under the worry signs is the writer's own summary. The facts say red, inflamed or ulcerated, and don't mention swelling.

"ส่วนใหญ่เกิดจากเม็ดทรายที่ติดแผ่นแม่เหล็ก ... " – the facts list several common causes with no ranking; 'mostly' sand in the pad is not supported. The FAQ repeats it as "ส่วนใหญ่เป็นเพราะมีทรายหรือเศษกรวดติดอยู่".
"ส่องดูกระจกทุกด้าน" – the facts say check the panels regularly under good light. 'Every side' is a mild embellishment.
"ปล่อยไว้แล้วหมุนตู้ ... จะดีกว่าการขัด" is framed as 'some sources'; the facts attribute it to one source (WikiHow).
"ส่วนด้านนอกใช้ได้" – outside use of glass cleaner is supported only if sprayed on a cloth, which the guide states; fine.
"ใช้ใบมีดโลหะ... ที่ขูดที่ใช้ใบมีดสแตนเลสและมีดโกนขูดตู้" – the Tetra GS 45 and ADA Pro Razor product names are dropped and generalised; this is acceptable but not exact.
"เม็ดทรายที่ติดแผ่นแม่เหล็ก ... อุปกรณ์ขัดที่หยาบเกินไป" – 'abrasive tools too coarse' is a loose generalisation of metal scrubbers.
"ขูดตะไคร่ด้านในก่อนเปลี่ยนน้ำ ... ใช้น้ำส้มสายชูขาวกับคราบหินปูนโดยไม่ให้หยดลงตู้ที่มีน้ำ" – the intro is consistent with the facts.

"แหล่งข้อมูลพูดถึงความเข้มข้นไม่ตรงกัน ... ทั้งสองแหล่งตรงกันว่าควรเป็นน้ำส้มสายชูขาว" – the facts only say undiluted white vinegar for stains and diluted white vinegar for cleaning the tank. They don't say both sources agree. The guide infers this.

"หลังขัดด้วยกระดาษทรายแล้ว ให้ขัดเงาต่อด้วยน้ำยาขัดพลาสติก" - the facts say sand then use plastic polish, but only in the context of acrylic tanks; the Micro-Mesh step list itself does not include it. This is a mild stretch.
"ถ้าใช้แม่เหล็กสำหรับกระจกบางกับกระจกหนา แรงดูดจะไม่พอและแม่เหล็กจะหลุดง่าย" - the facts say it grips poorly and slips, which matches closely. This is fine.

"ตรวจกระจกทุกด้านเป็นประจำ" and the "ตรวจหลังทำความสะอาด" section - the post-cleaning checklist (re-check with a fingernail, look for new faint scratches) is the guide's own addition. The facts do not give it as a post-cleaning procedure.
"ถ้ายังสะดุดอยู่แสดงว่ารอยยังลึก" - the fingernail test is applied to a scratch after polishing, which the facts do not say.
"ย้ายปลากลับ" and "ล้างน้ำส้มสายชูออกให้หมดทุกจุดก่อนเติมน้ำ" - the checklist and the general advice to rinse are loosely supported. The extension to polish residue is not in the facts.
"รอยตื้น: ... ถูน้ำยาขัดเบา ๆ เป็นวงกลม" - this matches the facts for glass, so it is fine.

The chloramine bullet in the prevention section is placed there as advice, and the facts do not tie it to cleaning. It is a fact about tap water that has little to do with the topic, so it is tangential but not wrong.
"cá nhịn được ít nhất khoảng một tuần" (FAQ): facts say most fish go about a week (or days to weeks), not "at least" a week.
"Mất điện dưới 2 giờ thì thường không sao" / "cá chắc là qua được một đêm": facts say fish should make it overnight if aeration or circulation is provided; the guide's 'chắc là' is a bit stronger.
"loại thường bán phần lớn tự chuyển sang pin": facts say most UPS switch to battery automatically, not about what is sold commonly.
"Mất điện vài tiếng thì có thể đun nước bằng bếp ga" matches, but "Nhớ chừa chỗ cho thoáng khí" is applied to the closed-lid wrap; fine, though 'đóng kín cửa phòng' is only from the timeline.
"nước bên trong có thể đã hết oxy và chứa đầy chất độc" (FAQ): 'full of toxins' is stronger than the facts' ammonia/hydrogen sulfide build-up in long outages.
"Một người chơi ở TP.HCM kể rằng thay pin mới rẻ hơn mua máy mới": supported; but 'Bộ lưu điện thì chạy lọc được lâu' is fine.
"Để cá yên. Trong tối cá dùng ít oxy hơn": supported; 'Lúc đó có ba mối nguy' fine.
"Tạo oxy trước khi cá bắt đầu đớp khí" step ordering: facts give this only for the scoop pour method, guide generalises to all methods.

"Trên một tuần | Nhờ tiệm cá..." is in the facts, fine; but "Mất điện vài tiếng thì ... Túi chườm nước nóng cũng dùng được" is OK. Problem: "Có máy sủi chạy pin thì gắn cục sủi vào chạy luôn" is fine.
"Không có bộ lưu điện, mất điện khoảng 1 giờ" is supported, but the table lists it under a keeper's suggestion mixed with the 'Mất điện quá 2 giờ' row; minor.
"Bộ lưu điện thì để chạy lọc" is an unsupported recommendation (facts only say a UPS can run the filter).

"Mất điện lâu thì chạy máy sủi dùng pin" in the intro is roughly supported by the timeline, but "Một nguồn nói cá chủ yếu sống được vài ngày" garbles "Most fish can survive days or even weeks" (minor).
"Nếu có sủi hoặc có nước chuyển động thì cá thường qua được một đêm" adds 'water movement' loosely; facts say 'aeration or circulation', acceptable.
"Ở TP.HCM, một người chơi kể pin thay mới rẻ hơn mua máy mới" is supported.
"Rút hẳn phích lọc ra. Có điện lại mà lọc tự chạy..." is supported.
"Dưới 2 giờ ... không lọc cũng thường không sao" is supported.
"đóng kín cửa phòng" for 4–8 hours: facts say 'keep the room closed', supported.
"Cá chịu được vài tiếng" and "lọc coi như hết tác dụng" are supported by the Sri Lankan source.
"Nước mát giữ được nhiều oxy hơn" appears in the shading advice; the facts tie it to the battery pump/cooler water, not shading. This is only a mild stretch.
"vệ sinh lọc trước rồi đo amoniac" in the intro: the facts say clean the filter, and test after power returns. The order and the pairing are loosely inferred.
"Cúp quá một tuần: nhờ tiệm cá giữ cá giùm" is supported, but the table's blank cells for 8–24h and 24h+ are fine. No issue.
"Pin hết thì thay pin mới rẻ hơn mua máy mới" is generalised from one keeper's prices (150k battery vs 350k pump).
"Cá nhịn được khoảng một tuần" in the FAQ is stated as fact. The sources differ (days to weeks, about a week).
"Nếu có sủi hoặc có cách cho nước lưu thông thì cá chắc là qua được một đêm" is stronger than the source, which says fish should make it overnight.
"Có thể trữ sẵn viên oxy" and the pond advice are supported. The "Sưởi 10 W tốn điện ít hơn hẳn" claim is also supported.
"Bộ lưu điện chạy lọc thì được lâu" in the FAQ is slightly stronger than "can run the filter for a long time". It is acceptable.
"vì nước trong lọc có thể đã hết oxy và chứa amoniac, hydro sunfua" combines two separate facts. It is a mild merge.
"Bộ lưu điện chỉ nên để chạy lọc": the facts only say not to run the heater from a UPS and that a UPS can run the filter. "Only for the filter" goes slightly beyond them.
"Mua về thì chạy thử ngay và thỉnh thoảng kiểm tra lại": the facts only report that not testing a new pump is a common mistake. "Check it again from time to time" is added advice.
"khi về thì thay 25–50% nước": the facts say to change 25–50% if you are away during the outage. They don't say to do it on returning home.
"Betta hoang chịu được nước ấm ở giữa dải 80–89°F": facts only say mid-80s °F; the 80–89°F range is invented.

"Ca nặng chết vì thiếu oxy do mang bị hoại tử" is supported, but "Đây là lúc mang đã bị phá nặng" and "Bệnh quay lại... là dấu hiệu trị chưa đủ lâu, hoặc bể chính chưa được trị" are the writer's own inferences.
"Đồng là thuốc chính để trị nhung": the facts do not say copper is the main drug.

"Một nguồn khác cũng nói 7 ngày tối hẳn có thể giúp thêm" is attributed to a separate source, but it is the same claim as the Aquarium Co-op one; the facts don't present it as an independent confirmation.
"Cho muối hột vào" (step 5) and "Muối ăn thường" table row: the facts say "aquarium salt" and plain sodium chloride; "muối hột" is a different product.

"Thuốc nào bảng dưới không ghi liều thì dùng liều theo nhãn" and the Vietnamese-products section avoid names, which is fine. But the "Ở Việt Nam" section claims products are "bán sẵn cho betta" and that "có loại dành cho cá chịu xanh malachite kém", which is only loosely supported.
"Nhiệt độ tụt khoảng 15°F trong vòng một giờ" is fine, but "Chúng... tự bơi đi tìm cá để bám" and "Có con nằm sát mặt nước đớp khí" are mild embellishments.
"Bệnh nhung có thể bám hình túi" in the FAQ garbles the facts: it is the trophont that is sac-shaped.
The table attributes sources as "FAO" and "Một nguồn thú y thủy sản"; the facts give only source numbers, so these attributions are invented.
"Cá vàng và cá ngựa vằn dễ mắc bệnh hơn" is supported, but "Betta hoang... cá nước đen" is fine; "Nên đưa cá sang bể riêng để trị" for shrimp tanks is the writer's own recommendation.
"Betta hoang chịu được mức giữa 80 °F một thời gian" – facts say mid-80s °F, not 80s/mid-80; this is a changed number.
"Cá bị stress vì vậy cũng có thể yếu sức đề kháng đi" – fine, but "cá mè vinh con" for Puntius gonionotus is a translation addition (minor, supported species).
"Thuốc nào không có liều trong bảng dưới đây thì dùng liều theo nhãn" – the writer's rule, acceptable; but listing methylene blue, formalin, acriflavine as drugs is supported.

"Một nguồn chuyên betta hoang dùng cách này cho betta hoang, giữ nước từ 84 °F trở lên trong 30 ngày" – facts tie 30 days at 84°F+ to CopperSafe at about 5 ml per 5 gallons; guide leaves out the dose but links it to chelated copper generally, a slight generalization.
"Một hướng dẫn nuôi cá và Wikipedia nói ký sinh trùng cần ánh sáng" – supported (source 0 says Aquarium Co-op and Wikipedia).
"Thuốc chỉ giết được con non đang bơi... nên thường phải dùng thuốc nhiều lần" – supported.
"Giai đoạn nặng thì cá thở khó, bỏ ăn, có con nằm sát mặt nước đớp khí" – supported.
"Đây là dấu hiệu hay gặp" and "Cá cụp vây và lờ đờ" – supported.
"Khử trùng ống hút, vợt và bàn chải" – supported.

"Xem kỹ lại các dấu hiệu ở trên. Nếu có kính hiển vi thì soi mẫu..." – first-aid step 4 is the writer's addition, not a fact-based claim; also the immediate action of raising the temperature to 29°C is listed in first aid, though facts place it under treatment steps (minor).

"Cho muối hột vào." and the first-aid step ordering: facts say 'aquarium salt'; 'muối hột' (coarse salt) is a different product; also placing 'add salt' as an immediate step sits against the sources saying salt has little effect.
"Giảm đèn hoặc tắt hẳn đèn." in immediate steps: facts say 'dim or turn off lights' but the guide gives this as a plain action while also presenting darkness as disputed; minor tension.

"Nước chua thì nên dùng đồng chelate." is supported, but "Đồng độc hơn khi nước chua" is stated generally and then linked to the 0.3 ppm Puntius example; the source only gives it for freshwater below pH 7.

"Đã tách cá bệnh ra thì trị luôn cả hai bể." in the intro is fine, but "Thấy cá ... thở gấp thì ... bắt đầu trị" implies treating on sight without diagnosis; the facts stress confirming against ich by microscope (small generalisation).

"Bệnh nặng thường giết cá vì ngạt, do mang bị hoại tử" combines two sources; supported, but "Cá con, cá già, betta hoang và cá nước đen là những con cần để mắt kỹ hơn" is the writer's recommendation, not a fact.
